hyo-.definition:
A prexif used in anatomy, and generally denoting connection
   with the hyoid bone or arch; as, hyoglossal, hyomandibular, hyomental,
   etc.

hyodeoxycholic acid.translation: [化] 猪去氧胆酸; 猪脱氧胆酸; 3,6-二羟基胆烷酸

hyoglossal.definition:
a. Pertaining to or connecting the tongue and hyodean
   arch; as, the hyoglossal membrane.
a. Of or pertaining to the hyoglossus muscle.

hyoglossus.definition:
n. A flat muscle on either side of the tongue, connecting
   it with the hyoid bone.

hyoid.definition:
n. a U-shaped bone at the base of the tongue that supports the tongue muscles
a. of or relating to the hyoid bone
hyoid.translation:
a. 舌骨的
n. 舌骨

hyoid bars.translation: [医] 舌骨板(第二鳃弓,舌骨弓)

hyomandibular.definition:
a. Pertaining both to the hyoidean arch and the
   mandible or lower jaw; as, the hyomandibular bone or cartilage, a
   segment of the hyoid arch which connects the lower jaw with the skull
   in fishes.
n. The hyomandibular bone or cartilage.

hyomental.definition:
a. Between the hyoid bone and the lower jaw, pertaining to
   them; suprahyoid; submaxillary; as, the hyomental region of the front
   of the neck.

hyopereurypia.translation: 脸裂过大, 眼过度开大

hyopharyngeus.translation: [医] 咽中缩肌, 舌骨咽肌

hyoscine.definition: n an alkaloid with anticholinergic effects that is used as a sedative and to treat nausea and to dilate the pupils in ophthalmic procedures
hyoscine.translation:
n. 东莨菪碱, 瞳孔扩散剂
[化] 莨菪胺; 天仙子碱; 东莨菪碱

hyoscine chorea.translation: [医] 莨菪硷中毒性舞蹈病

hyoscyamin.translation: n. (草本植物)黑茛菪的干叶(可作解痉药和镇静药)

hyoscyamine.definition: n a poisonous crystalline alkaloid (isometric with atropine but more potent); used to treat excess motility of the gastrointestinal tract

hyoscyamus.definition: n genus of poisonous herbs: henbane
hyoscyamus.translation: n. (草本植物)黑茛菪的干叶(可作解痉药和镇静药)

hyosternal.definition:
a. Between the hyoid bone and the sternum, or pertaining
   to them; infrahyoid; as, the hyosternal region of the neck.
a. Pertaining to the hyosternum of turtles.

hyostylic.definition:
a. Having the mandible suspended by the hyomandibular, or
   upper part of the hyoid arch, as in fishes, instead of directly
   articulated with the skull as in mammals; -- said of the skull.
